option_description: Attests that the deploying environment cryptographically verifies a SLSA provenance attestation (or equivalent signed in-toto attestation) on every artifact before admission, with the signature chained to a pinned builder identity, OIDC issuer, and expected source repo/ref — never admitting an artifact pulled by tag alone.
security_impact: Triggers exposure "Unsigned/unverified artifact admitted (SLSA bypass)" — this attribute is the sole OR-condition, firing when artifact_supply_chain_signed_provenance_verified is false (T1195.002 Compromise Software Supply Chain). Without verified provenance the deploy channel will accept a tampered or substituted image as legitimate.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Run cosign verify-attestation against a representative production image, pinning the expected builder workflow identity and OIDC issuer; success with a SLSA provenance predicate that matches the expected source repo/ref proves the verification path is wired correctly.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Verification passes AND predicate buildType / builder.id / externalParameters.sourceRepo / sourceRef match policy (secure). Failure or 'no matching attestations' = insecure.
how_to_obtain.source: SLSA v1.0 Verifying Artifacts spec; Sigstore cosign verify-attestation reference

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the cluster admission policies (Sigstore policy-controller ClusterImagePolicy or Kyverno verifyImages) for a SLSA provenance verification step pinned to issuer/identity and source repo; audit-only or absent policy means provenance is never enforced.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A policy exists requiring --type slsaprovenance with predicateType https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1 and pinned issuer/identity in enforce mode (secure); no policy or audit-only mode (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Sigstore policy-controller overview; Kyverno verifyImages sigstore docs

option_description: Attestation that every commit on the deploy ref is cryptographically signed (GPG, SSH, S/MIME, or keyless Sigstore/gitsign) and the signature is verifiable against an authorised identity.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions for exposure "Unsigned commits reach deploy branch" — fires when commits_signed is false (T1195.002 Compromise Software Supply Chain). Unsigned commits ride the channel into prod as unattributable changes.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Run git log with signature display on the deploy ref over a meaningful window (e.g. last 20 commits) and confirm every commit shows a valid signature from an authorised key.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: All recent commits show 'Good signature' from a known signer (secure); any 'no signature' / 'unknown signature' line (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: GitHub Docs — About commit signature verification; Sigstore Gitsign docs

how_to_obtain.instruction: On developer workstations confirm git is configured to sign by default and uses a recognised key format — proves the team's tooling produces signatures rather than relying on ad-hoc per-commit flags.
how_to_obtain.command: git config --get commit.gpgsign && git config --get gpg.format
how_to_obtain.expected_output: commit.gpgsign=true; gpg.format=ssh or x509 (secure). Unset (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: GitHub Docs — Signing commits / Telling Git about your signing key; Sigstore Gitsign docs

option_description: Attestation that the repository ruleset / branch protection on the deploy ref enforces the required_signatures rule so unsigned commits are rejected at push time rather than relying on contributor discipline.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions for exposure "Unsigned commits reach deploy branch" — fires when required_signatures_enforced_on_deploy_ref is false (T1195.002). Even if developers sign by convention, without the platform rule a single unsigned push lands on prod.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the GitHub Rules API for the deploy ref and filter for a required_signatures rule entry — its presence is what enforces the policy server-side.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A JSON object describing a required_signatures rule (secure); empty output / no match (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: GitHub Docs — Available rules for rulesets; About commit signature verification

how_to_obtain.instruction: Open the repository's Rulesets / Branch protection settings in the GitHub UI for the deploy ref and visually confirm 'Require signed commits' is enabled.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Repo → Settings → Rules → Rulesets → <deploy-ref ruleset> → Branch rules → 'Require signed commits' checked
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 'Require signed commits' is enabled and the ruleset is in Active enforcement (secure); rule absent or in Evaluate-only mode (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: GitHub Docs — Available rules for rulesets

option_description: Attestation that the CI/CD pipeline authenticates to each target environment with a distinct, short-lived, federated workload identity (e.g. GitHub Actions OIDC pinned by sub/audience to repo:<owner>/<repo>:environment:<env>, federated to per-environment cloud roles) rather than a single long-lived static cloud credential shared across all environments.
security_impact: Sole OR-condition for exposure "Shared long-lived CI key compromises all environments" — fires when cicd_pipeline_identity_per_environment_no_long_lived_keys is false (T1078 Valid Accounts). A leaked shared key collapses blast-radius to one token across every environment.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inventory CI environments and workflows: confirm separate GitHub environments exist with environment-scoped secrets/roles and that deploy workflows declare permissions.id-token: write plus an environment: <name> on the deploy job.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Separate environments with environment-scoped roles AND id-token: write on the deploy job (secure). A single org-wide long-lived cloud key in repo secrets (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: GitHub Docs — Configuring OpenID Connect in Cloud providers; Google Cloud Workload Identity Federation with deployment pipelines

how_to_obtain.instruction: Dump the cloud trust policy attached to each deploy role and confirm the sub/audience claim pins to repo:<owner>/<repo>:environment:<env> for the specific environment — wildcard subs are the smoking gun for a shared identity.
how_to_obtain.command: aws iam get-role --role-name <deploy-role> --query 'AssumeRolePolicyDocument' (or: gcloud iam workload-identity-pools providers describe <provider> --location=global --workload-identity-pool=<pool>)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Trust policy pins sub/aud to repo:<owner>/<repo>:environment:<env> per environment (secure). Wildcard sub or any-repo trust (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Google Cloud — Workload Identity Federation with deployment pipelines; GitHub Docs OIDC

option_description: Attests that the deploy workflow / environment is gated so it can only fire from a protected branch (or protected tag) — i.e. GitHub environment deployment_branch_policy.protected_branches=true, or an equivalent ref restriction in the CI platform.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions for exposure "Deploy triggered from unprotected branch / fork" — fires when deploy_ref_protected_branch_only is false (T1195.002, T1078). A push to any branch or a fork PR could otherwise drive the deploy flow.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the environment's deployment-branch-policies and confirm protected_branches=true (or a tightly scoped custom allow-list of refs).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: deployment_branch_policy.protected_branches=true (secure); custom_branch_policies allowing any ref or no policy at all (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: GitHub Docs — Deployments and environments (environment protection rules)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Open the prod-equivalent environment in the GitHub UI and visually confirm the Deployment branches setting is set to 'Protected branches only' (or a narrowly scoped pattern).
how_to_obtain.navigation: Repo → Settings → Environments → <prod> → Deployment branches and tags → 'Protected branches only'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 'Protected branches only' is selected (secure); 'No restriction' (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: GitHub Docs — Deployments and environments

option_description: Attests that the deployment environment (e.g. prod) has required human reviewers configured as an environment protection rule, so a deploy cannot proceed without explicit approval — even from a protected branch.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions for exposure "Deploy triggered from unprotected branch / fork" — fires when deploy_required_reviewers_configured is false (T1195.002, T1078). Without it the channel runs unattended on every qualifying push.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Pull the environment object via the GitHub API and inspect protection_rules for a required_reviewers entry with non-empty reviewers — and verify reviewers are not just the deploying actor.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A required_reviewers protection rule listing one or more humans/teams (secure); no required_reviewers entry or self-approval allowed (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: GitHub Docs — Deployments and environments (environment protection rules)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Open the environment in the GitHub UI and confirm the 'Required reviewers' protection rule is enabled with at least one reviewer who is not the deploying actor.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 'Required reviewers' enabled with named reviewers (secure); disabled (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: GitHub Docs — Deployments and environments

option_description: Attests that secrets traversing the deployment channel are injected into the running workload at deploy/start time from an external secret store (Vault Agent, Secrets-Store CSI, External Secrets Operator) — never embedded in the image, ConfigMap, Dockerfile, or build artifact carried by the flow.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions for exposure "Secrets baked into artifact instead of runtime-injected" — fires when secrets_injected_at_runtime_not_baked_in is false (T1552.001 Unsecured Credentials: Credentials in Files). Baked secrets propagate to every environment and every image puller.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Scan the production image's layer history and run a secret-scanner over the image to detect credentials embedded at build time.
how_to_obtain.command: docker history --no-trunc <image> | grep -iE 'PASSWORD|TOKEN|SECRET|KEY=' ; trivy image --scanners secret <image>
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No matches and trivy reports no secret findings (secure); any hit (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Sigstore/Chainguard image-hygiene guidance; CIS Docker / Kubernetes Benchmark

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect a representative production pod spec for Vault sidecar annotations, Secrets-Store CSI volumes, or ExternalSecret references — the canonical runtime-injection markers.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secrets-Store CSI volume, Vault sidecar inject annotation, or ExternalSecret reference present (secure); env values hard-coded or pulled from a baked ConfigMap (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: HashiCorp Vault Kubernetes sidecar tutorial; Secrets-Store CSI driver docs

option_description: Attests that the deploy pipeline runs a blocking secret scanner (gitleaks, trufflehog, trivy --scanners secret, detect-secrets) on the artifact AND on rendered Helm/Kustomize manifests before applying — catching credentials that slipped past commit-time hooks.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions for exposure "Secrets baked into artifact instead of runtime-injected" — fires when secret_scanning_enabled is false (T1552.001). Without a deploy-time scan, leaked credentials slip through the channel undetected.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Grep CI workflow definitions for a blocking secret-scanner step (gitleaks, trufflehog, trivy --scanners secret, detect-secrets) running on the artifact and on rendered manifests.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A blocking step running gitleaks / trufflehog / trivy --scanners secret on the artifact and Helm/Kustomize render output (secure); no scan or warn-only continue-on-error step (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-218 SSDF PW.7 (Review and analyze code); GitHub Advanced Security secret-scanning docs

how_to_obtain.instruction: Pull the last N successful pipeline runs that landed on prod and confirm the secret-scan step actually executed and exited zero with a clean report — a step that exists in YAML but is skipped doesn't enforce anything.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Recent runs show the secret-scan job executed with a clean exit and the next job ran only on its success (secure); job skipped or step is informational only (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Attestation that the deployment channel (registry pull, kube-apiserver call, GitOps webhook) is carried over TLS 1.2+ end-to-end with no cleartext fallback.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions for exposure "Cleartext or downgraded TLS on registry/apiserver channel" — fires when flow_tls_encrypted is false (T1557 Adversary-in-the-Middle). Cleartext on the deploy flow opens classic AiTM artifact substitution.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Probe each hop the deploy flow traverses (registry, kube-apiserver, GitOps webhook) with openssl s_client forced to TLS 1.2 and inspect the negotiated protocol, cert chain, and SAN.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: TLS 1.2/1.3 handshake; cert chain trusted; SAN matches host (secure). Handshake fails / SSLv3/TLS1.0 negotiated / cleartext port reachable (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-52r2 (TLS Implementation); Mozilla Server-Side TLS guidance

how_to_obtain.instruction: Run testssl.sh against each deploy-flow hop with HIGH severity filter to catch downgrade and weak-cipher findings beyond what s_client surfaces.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No HIGH severity findings; modern cipher suites only (secure); HIGH findings such as cleartext fallback or TLS 1.0/1.1 acceptance (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Mozilla Server-Side TLS guidance

option_description: Attestation that the deploying client strictly validates the server certificate (trusted CA chain, SAN match, no self-signed acceptance) on every connection in the deploy flow.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions for exposure "Cleartext or downgraded TLS on registry/apiserver channel" — fires when server_certificate_validated is false (T1557 Adversary-in-the-Middle). Accepting self-signed/unvalidated TLS lets an on-path attacker terminate the channel and substitute the artifact or deploy verb.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the kubeconfig and any deploy-client config (helm, argocd CLI, docker/containerd registry config) for --insecure-skip-tls-verify, insecureSkipVerify: true, or insecure-registries entries that bypass validation.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No matches (secure); any 'true' / non-empty insecure-registries entry on a deploy-flow client (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

how_to_obtain.instruction: From a deploy-runner-equivalent host probe each hop with a known-bad (self-signed) cert in front to confirm the client refuses to connect — a positive test that validation is on.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Verify return code: 0 (ok) and SAN matches host (secure); 'verify error' or self-signed accepted in the client config (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-52r2 (TLS Implementation); Mozilla Server-Side TLS guidance

option_description: Attestation that every manifest crossing this deployment flow references its artifact by immutable digest (sha256:...) rather than a mutable tag (:latest, :prod, :stable).
security_impact: Sole OR-condition for exposure "Mutable tag swap after verification (no digest pinning)" — fires when artifact_references_immutable_digest_pinned is false (T1036 Masquerading, T1195.002). A registry can repoint the tag post-verification so restarting pods pull a substituted image — what policy verified is no longer what runs.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate every running container's image reference across all namespaces and filter out anything that lacks an @sha256: digest — non-empty output names every offending manifest.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Empty output: all images digest-pinned (secure). Any image without @sha256:... (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: SLSA v1.0 Verifying Artifacts — 'compare artifact digest to provenance statement subject' presumes digest pinning

how_to_obtain.instruction: Grep rendered Helm/Kustomize output and the GitOps manifest repo for image: references that end in a tag rather than a digest — the source-of-truth view of what the flow actually applies.
how_to_obtain.file_path: Rendered Helm/Kustomize output / GitOps manifest repo
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No matches (secure); any tag-only image: line (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Attests that deploy events crossing this flow are streamed to a central, out-of-account audit log/SIEM, so post-incident attribution does not depend on logs the deploying identity can edit.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions for exposure "No central audit of deploy events" — fires when centralized_log_aggregation is false (T1562.008 Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Cloud Logs, T1070 Indicator Removal). Without central aggregation, deploy events never reach a tamper-evident store.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the SIEM for Kubernetes/cloud deploy events (create deployments, UpdateService, image-pull events) over the last 7 days and confirm ingestion includes actor identity and artifact digest.
how_to_obtain.command: Check SIEM ingestion: query for cloudtrail/CloudAudit/Kubernetes audit events with verb=create resource=deployments OR eventName=UpdateService over last 7d
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Deploy events present, retained per policy, with actor identity and artifact digest visible (secure). Missing source, audit pipeline disabled, or events absent (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Kubernetes audit logs SIEM integration practice (Exabeam/LogRhythm guidance); Wiz 'What is SIEM' cloud-native logging

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the kube-apiserver audit policy to confirm deploy-relevant verbs are logged at RequestResponse granularity rather than Metadata-only.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Policy logs RequestResponse for deployments.apps, rollouts, jobs (secure); audit policy absent or Metadata-only on deploy verbs (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Kubernetes documentation on audit logging

option_description: Attests that the audit log destination is tamper-evident — write-once / append-only / cryptographically chained — and hosted in an account the deploying identity cannot edit or delete from.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions for exposure "No central audit of deploy events" — fires when audit_log_tamper_evident is false (T1562.008, T1070). Without WORM/cross-account isolation, a cluster-admin or compromised deploy identity can erase its tracks even when forwarding is on.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the log destination's storage configuration (S3 Object Lock retention, Loki immutable backend, Splunk frozen-bucket policy) and the IAM model that owns it — confirm the deploying account holds no delete or retention-override rights.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: WORM/append-only storage (e.g. S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode) in an account separated from the deploying identity's blast radius (secure); deploying account can delete or shorten retention (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

how_to_obtain.instruction: For AWS-backed audit destinations, inspect the S3 bucket's Object Lock configuration directly to confirm a retention mode is set.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ObjectLockConfiguration with ObjectLockEnabled=Enabled and a default retention rule (secure); 'Object Lock configuration does not exist' (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Attests that the deployment flow runs continuous reconciliation (GitOps controller such as Argo CD selfHeal / Flux, or scheduled terraform plan -detailed-exitcode wired to alerts) against a declared source-of-truth, so any out-of-band change to running config is detected and alerted.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions for exposure "Out-of-band drift in running config undetected" — fires when drift_detection_enabled is false (T1098.006 Account Manipulation: Additional Container Cluster Roles, T1562 Impair Defenses). Without reconciliation, direct kubectl/console changes go unnoticed.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Search the GitOps configuration tree for selfHeal / automated sync policies — the marker that the controller is actively reverting drift rather than just rendering.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: syncPolicy.automated.selfHeal=true OR drift alerts wired to SIEM (secure); manual sync only with no monitoring (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Configuration drift detection / SIEM correlation guidance (CoreView, Entro)

how_to_obtain.instruction: List Argo CD apps (or Flux Kustomizations) and confirm the controller is healthy and its sync policy is automated; a controller in degraded/manual state is not detecting drift.
how_to_obtain.command: argocd app list -o wide   # or: flux get kustomizations
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Apps listed with SYNC POLICY = Auto and HEALTH = Healthy (secure); SYNC POLICY = Manual or controller not installed (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Attests that, at assessment time, the running configuration of the target environment is in sync with the declared source-of-truth baseline (argocd app diff / flux diff / terraform plan reports no differences).
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions for exposure "Out-of-band drift in running config undetected" — fires when running_config_matches_baseline is false (T1098.006, T1562). Even with reconciliation configured, drift currently present means it is not being evicted in practice.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Run the reconciler's diff at assessment time against the production app/stack and confirm no differences — the point-in-time check that drift is not currently persisting.
how_to_obtain.command: argocd app diff <app> --refresh   # or: flux diff kustomization <name>   # or: terraform plan -detailed-exitcode
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Exit code 0 / 'no differences' (secure, in sync). Non-zero diff = drift currently present (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Argo CD / Flux docs (industry pattern referenced in Microsoft 365 and CoreView drift-management guidance)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the last 7 days of reconciler alerts / drift notifications for unresolved entries on the production app — open drift findings are running-config-vs-baseline divergence by definition.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No open drift alerts on the prod app (secure); one or more unresolved drift entries (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge
